title: t18795: fix(pulse): make the draft-checkpoint dispatch cooldown take effect across cycles
body:
## Task


Make the GH#34526 draft-checkpoint dispatch cooldown actually take effect. Today almost every candidate pinned by an unchanged worker draft PR repeats the full `dispatch_with_dedup` ceremony (33–135s each) every pulse cycle. That starves the dispatch round of launchable candidates.

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

Make the GH#34526 draft-checkpoint dispatch cooldown actually take effect. Today almost every candidate pinned by an unchanged worker draft PR repeats the full `dispatch_with_dedup` ceremony (33–135s each) every pulse cycle. That starves the dispatch round of launchable candidates.

## Why (observed evidence, 2026-10-29 06:23–22:03Z, one 20-slot runner)

- `pulse-cycle-index.jsonl`, last 24 cycles: 0–5 dispatched and 0–3 of 20 workers active per cycle; cycle durations up to 5453s. Candidates are repeatedly deferred with `cycle budget 579s below per-candidate floor 600s; stage not started` (GH#34428).
- `pulse.log` (last 40k lines): 224 `DISPATCH_BLOCK_REASON reason=dedup*` blocks, 139 of them `WORKER_DRAFT_CHECKPOINT`. Failed `dispatch_candidate_*` stages for draft-pinned issues used 8148s of the 12381s spent in all failed candidate stages (66%).
- Continuation-helper verdicts in the same window: 88 `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: PR #N ... has no current stall release`, 7 `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS`, 4 `... is assigned`.
- `draft checkpoint cooldown skipped` (enumeration filter) appears 0 times. `cross-cycle ownership block:worker_draft_checkpoint_*` appears 0 times. `~/.aidevops/logs/dispatch-negative-cache/` holds 96 `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` records and only 8 `worker_draft_checkpoint_cooldown` records.

## Root cause

1. **Classifier never sees the verdict.** `_dispatch_record_nonzero_dispatch_result` records the cooldown only when `_dispatch_checkpoint_cooldown_eligible "$recent_lines"` matches. `_dispatch_candidate_recent_lines` (`pulse-dispatch-lib-capacity.sh`) keeps only lines with both the exact `#<issue>` token and the repo slug. `pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh` prints `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED: PR #<pr> in <repo> has no current stall release` and `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS: PR #<pr> in <repo> ...` keyed only by PR number, so both are filtered out. Only the `issue #N ... is assigned` variant reaches the classifier. `test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh` stubs `_dispatch_candidate_recent_lines`, which hid this.
2. **TTL shorter than the cycle gap.** The cooldown defaults to 1800s (cap 3600s), and `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` is capped at 1800s. Full dispatch cycles start 30–120 min apart (`cache_prime` at 11:45, 12:17, 12:46, 14:12, 14:45, 15:49, 16:31, 16:46, 18:17, 18:52, 19:22, 21:23, 21:53Z), so even a recorded hint has usually expired by the next cycle.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`: append ` issue=#<issue>` to the verdict lines `BLOCKED_CHECKPOINT_ATTENTION_EXISTS` (two sites), `STALLED_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_SKIPPED` (`has no current stall release` and `runner_capability_unmet` variants) and `PR_CHECKPOINT_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED ... launch failed rc=`. Existing consumers match by prefix or substring.
2. `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh` `_dispatch_checkpoint_cooldown_eligible`: also refuse windows containing a `launch failed rc=` continuation, which is a transient capacity/launch outcome. Now visible, it must never be cooled.
3. `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh` `_dispatch_negative_cache_reason`: for `worker_draft_checkpoint_cooldown` only, use a longer quiet-revision TTL (`AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_CHECKPOINT_QUIET_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`, default 21600, cap 86400, 0 disables). It applies only when the candidate is unassigned and the record was written at least `AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_CHECKPOINT_QUIET_AFTER_SECONDS` (default 14400) after the issue revision it is keyed to. Otherwise keep today's base cooldown. Leave `worker_draft_checkpoint_blocked` and every other reason unchanged.

### Safety argument for step 3

The cooldown reader already requires the exact issue `updatedAt` and label set. Every cooled outcome (no stall release, attention already posted, approved-continuation target rejected, runner capability self-release) is decided by issue comments/labels or PR metadata, which change `updatedAt`. Two outcomes depend on time:

- **GH#34008 expired-claim continuation** (`_pcc_expired_claim_evidence`). Claims and leases are new issue comments, and ready leases default to 7200s (`AIDEVOPS_DISPATCH_READY_LEASE_TTL`). A record written at least 14400s after the revision therefore saw every claim at that revision already expired.
- **Layer 6 stale-assignment recovery** for assigned issues. This is why assigned candidates are excluded from the quiet TTL.

Transient continuation launch failures are excluded by step 2.

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib-candidates.sh
- .agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-lib.sh
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh

## Acceptance

- Real helper verdict lines written to `LOGFILE` reach `_dispatch_candidate_recent_lines` for the issue and record `worker_draft_checkpoint_cooldown`.
- A quiet, unassigned cooled candidate stays filtered past the base TTL. A candidate whose record is within the quiet horizon of its revision, or that is assigned, still expires at the base TTL. Base TTL 0 still disables.
- `launch failed rc=` windows are never cooled.
- No change to other negative-cache reasons.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-candidate-failure-reasons.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-stale-pr-continuation.sh`
- `shellcheck` on all changed scripts
- After deploy: `Dispatch enumeration: ... draft checkpoint cooldown skipped` appears in `pulse.log` across cycles, and per-cycle rc≠0 `dispatch_candidate_*` stage seconds in `pulse-stage-timings.log` fall.

</details>

body:
**Task ID:** `t18796` | **Status:** open
**Assignee:** @marcusquinn | **Logged:** 2026-10-29 | **Started:** 2026-10-29
**Tags:** `bug` `priority:high`

## Outcome

fix(full-loop): treat non-markdown data files under todo/ as deliverables, not planning-only

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr` treats any diff confined to `TODO.md` and `todo/**` as planning-only and writes `For #N` (`_diff_is_planning_only`, `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:196-209`, applied at `:242-246`). Data deliverables that a repository keeps under `todo/` (for example JSON/JSONL worklogs and specs) are not planning, so their PRs should use `Resolves #N`.

## Why

A managed repository stores award-enrichment worklogs and published specs under `todo/award-enrichment/log/**.jsonl` and `todo/award-enrichment/specs/**.json`. Every batch worker's data PR is entirely under `todo/`, so the helper writes `For #N`:

- 49 batch data PRs merged 2026-10-27 22:00 to 2026-10-29 22:30 UTC: 43 ended with `Resolves`, 6 with `For`. PR body edit history shows the `Resolves` ones were created with `For`/`Ref`/no keyword and hand-corrected by the worker after creation; the other 6 were not.
- Each uncorrected PR leaves its batch issue open after merge. Observed result: a "Partial Parent Closeout" comment on a non-parent issue and `worker_post_pr_handoff_unverified` cascade escalation `tier:standard → tier:thinking`, i.e. a second, more expensive dispatch for finished work.

PR #33990 (t18616) intended `For` only for planning diffs (`TODO.md`, briefs, plans). All planning artifacts under aidevops' own `todo/` are markdown (1071 `.md`; the only others are 2 `.sh`, 1 `.sql`, 1 `.gitkeep`).

## How

1. In `_diff_is_planning_only`, qualify only `TODO.md` and markdown under `todo/` (`todo/*.md` in a `case` pattern matches nested paths). Any other file under `todo/` (JSON, JSONL, CSV, scripts, etc.) makes the diff non-planning, so the default `Resolves` applies and the issue is labelled `status:in-review` as for any deliverable.
2. Keep the existing precedence: `--allow-parent-close` forces `Resolves`; parent-task and completion-bookkeeping still use `For`; empty diffs still do not qualify.
3. Extend the existing planning-only coverage in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` (it already exercises `_diff_is_planning_only`): `todo/x/y.jsonl` only → not planning; `todo/x/y.json` + `TODO.md` → not planning; `todo/tasks/t1-brief.md` + `TODO.md` → planning.

## Acceptance

- A diff of only `todo/**/*.jsonl`/`.json` produces `Resolves #N`; markdown-only `todo/**` and `TODO.md` diffs still produce `For #N`.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-runtime-risk.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-closed-issue-bookkeeping.sh` pass; ShellCheck clean on changed files.

title: test: test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh races the stub marker write (flaky CI)
body:
## What

Make `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` wait for the stub merge routine to *write* its marker, not just create it. The suite failed once in CI on an unrelated PR and passes locally and on `main`.

## Evidence

- On PR #36001 (head `d9d50ea4da`), Code Quality Analysis run `40971011332`, job "Framework Validation", step "Pulse-merge Regression Suites (GH#35943)" reported:
  `rc=1 0s test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` / `FAIL: merge routine did not receive the run subcommand` / `Pulse-merge suites: 49 run, 1 failed`.
- The PR does not touch `pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh` or the merge routine.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` passes locally on the same head. `main` (`fbdb2f65bd`) passed the same workflow minutes earlier.

## Why (root cause)

The stub at lines 48-54 runs `printf 'started:%s\n' "$*" >"${PULSE_MERGE_FIRST_TEST_MARKER}"`. The shell creates (truncates) the file before `printf` writes to it. The poll loop at lines 75-78 breaks on `[[ -f "$marker" ]]`, so on a slow runner line 80 can read an empty file and fail `started:run*`. The loop also gives up after 5 × 0.2 s.

## How

- Files Scope: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` only.
- Poll until the content matches, for example `[[ -s "$marker" && "$(<"$marker")" == started:* ]] && break`, with a longer bound such as 25 × 0.2 s. Keep the failure messages so a genuine regression still names the missing launch or the missing `run` argument.
- Optionally have the stub write atomically: `printf ... >"${marker}.tmp" && mv "${marker}.tmp" "$marker"`. The second (disabled-path) block at lines 84-100 uses the same marker; check it after the change.
- Do not change `pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`.

## Acceptance / Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` passes.
- It still fails if `_preflight_start_merge_first` is temporarily changed to omit `run` (check locally, then revert).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-first-nonblocking.sh` is clean.

title: Checkpoint history rejects stale-reset never-ready claims and manual-dispatch attempt rotation
body:
## What

A draft checkpoint stays unapprovable after successful later dispatch episodes. `approval-template` returns `intervening coordination is not fully released; no approval generated`, and `abort-pr-checkpoint-claim` returns `PR_CHECKPOINT_ABORT_DENIED reason=not_checkpoint_claim`. No supported route closes the history without discarding the draft.

Observed on a managed private repo (issue/PR numbers withheld). All events are by trusted MEMBER runners and none are edited. A read-only replay of `released_successor_history` found two framework-side rejections. A third is already covered by draft PR #35513 (unprefixed legacy attempt IDs).

### 1. Never-ready claim released by `stale_assignment_reset`

`DISPATCH_CLAIM` → `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch attempt_id=attempt:X` → (every expiry elapsed, no ready lease, no launch) → `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=stale_assignment_reset runner=<same runner> device=<claim device> stale_threshold_s=600`.

`advance_release` only recognises `claim_only_no_worker` and `blocked` as never-ready closers (GH#35331, GH#35683). This release falls through to `close_release`, which requires a ready lease, so the history becomes `None`. The claim owner's own stale-recovery release after expiry closes the claim exactly as firmly as a `blocked` release. It is still reported as an acknowledged successor and grants nothing on its own.

### 2. Attempt ID rotates between prelaunch and ready (manual dispatch + managed backend)

`DISPATCH_LEASE phase=prelaunch attempt_id=attempt:A` → `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=ready attempt_id=attempt:B` → `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=blocked` → `DISPATCH_LEASE phase=terminal attempt_id=attempt:B`. Same lease token, device, session and runner.

`advance_lease` locks the episode to the first lease's attempt ID, so the ready lease is rejected.

Root cause (producer): `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh` never allocates an attempt ID.
- `_dsi_renew_prelaunch_lease` posts the prelaunch lease with whatever `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_ID` the dispatcher inherited.
- `_dsi_launch_worker` leaves `AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_ID`/`AIDEVOPS_ATTEMPT_STARTED_AT` out of the worker argv.
- Since GH#35295 the worker is launched via `systemd-run --user` (`_dlw_exec_systemd_user_service`), which does not inherit the caller's environment. `_ensure_worker_attempt_identity` (`worker-lifecycle-common.sh`) then creates a fresh ID before the ready transition.

Pulse dispatch is not affected: `_dlw_begin_prelaunch` allocates one ID and `_dlw_nohup_launch` passes it in argv. Public evidence from the same day: pulse episodes ("Dispatching worker (deterministic)") keep one ID, while episodes without that comment rotate. The same runner switched from matching to rotating between v3.39.53 and v3.39.59, which is when the managed backend landed.

## How

1. `.agents/scripts/dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh`: allocate one canonical `attempt:` ID and start marker per manual dispatch (mirror `_dlw_begin_prelaunch`). Pass them explicitly to the prelaunch transition and to the worker argv so every backend receives them.
2. `.agents/scripts/pr_checkpoint_history.py`:
   - Accept `reason=stale_assignment_reset` as a never-ready closer with the same guards as `close_blocked_before_ready`. Bind the line's `device` to the claim's device, and report outcome `stale_reset_before_ready`.
   - Allow exactly one attempt rebind, at the first ready lease of an episode, before any launch or release. Lease token, session and runner must still match. Later leases/releases must match the ready attempt.
3. Tests: extend `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py` (pattern: `blocked_before_ready_fixture`) with positive and fail-closed cases.
4. Docs: `.agents/reference/checkpoint-revision-recovery.md` names the accepted never-ready outcomes.

## Acceptance

- The replayed history of the observed checkpoint (with #35513 applied for the legacy prefix) reconstructs fully, and `approval-template` generates a template listing the episodes as `released_successors`.
- Fail-closed: a rebind after a launch or a second rebind is rejected, as is a stale reset with a mismatched device, an unexpired lease, or a ready lease.
- `python3 .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-checkpoint-claim-only.py`, `test-pr-checkpoint-revision.py`, ShellCheck on the changed shell file.

title: aidevops_pre_edit_check MCP tool reports own session's worktree as owned by another session
body:
## What

The OpenCode MCP tool `aidevops_pre_edit_check` reports the calling session's own linked worktree as owned by "another active session/process" and exits 2. The same session's Bash call to `pre-edit-check.sh` in that worktree returns OK.

## Observed (aidevops v3.39.57, OpenCode v1.19.4, macOS)

1. `interactive-start-helper.sh --issue <N> --repo <owner/repo> --task "..." --auto-dispatch` claimed an issue and created a linked worktree. Ownership was registered at 00:54:32Z for session `ses_…` with the session's OpenCode PID.
2. About 10 minutes later, in the same session, `aidevops_pre_edit_check` with `workdir=<worktree>` returned:
   `BLOCKED: linked worktree is owned by another active session/process`, `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true`, `WORKTREE_OWNER_PID=<this session's opencode PID>`, `WORKTREE_OWNER_SESSION=<this session's ID>`, and `Worktree ownership transaction unavailable`.
3. In the same session, `printenv OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` returned exactly the reported owner session, and `ps -p <owner PID>` showed `opencode --session <same ID> --auto --agent Build+`.
4. `~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`, run through the Bash tool with the same workdir, printed `OK - In linked worktree on ref: <branch>`.

Likely cause: the MCP tool runs the check in the plugin/MCP process without the caller's session identity (`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` and/or owner PID ancestry). It therefore cannot match the stamp to its owner, and it also reports "ownership transaction unavailable".

## Impact

The tool wrongly tells an agent to create a second worktree for work it already owns, which invites duplicate worktrees or abandoned edits. The agent has to diagnose ownership by hand (env + ps) before using the shell-based check.

## Files

- MCP tool implementation of `aidevops_pre_edit_check` in the OpenCode plugin (exact path not verified; locate it with `rg -n "aidevops_pre_edit_check" .agents/` in the framework repo).
- `.agents/scripts/pre-edit-check.sh`: the worktree-ownership comparison and the source of "Worktree ownership transaction unavailable".

## Fix direction

Pass the caller's session identity (session ID and runtime PID) from the MCP tool into `pre-edit-check.sh`, using whatever environment variables the Bash path already provides. Treat a stamp whose owner session equals the caller's as owned by the caller. Keep failing closed for genuinely different live owners.

## Verification

- In one OpenCode session, create a worktree via `interactive-start-helper.sh`. Then call `aidevops_pre_edit_check` with that workdir and confirm exit 0.
- From a second session, call it on the same worktree and confirm it still blocks with `WORKTREE_OWNERSHIP_CONFLICT=true`.

title: t18797: Deflake bounded-operation timeout case: process_signal null under slow spawn
body:
## Task


Make the timeout case in `bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs` deterministic. Today the failure looks like this:

```
not ok 9 - failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success
location: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs:31:3
error: 'Expected "actual" to be strictly unequal to: null'   (line 39)
```

<details>
<summary>Full task brief and audit context</summary>

## Task Brief

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-30, interactive session (GH#35968 full-loop)
- **Evidence:** CI run https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/actions/runs/40979518374 (job 123815778665, `import-check` → Run plugin tests) failed on PR #36011. That PR does not touch bounded operations. The next run on the same PR passed without code changes to this area.

## What

Make the timeout case in `bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs` deterministic. Today the failure looks like this:

```
not ok 9 - failure, timeout, and scoped cancellation cannot appear as success
location: .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs:31:3
error: 'Expected "actual" to be strictly unequal to: null'   (line 39)
```

## Why

Required plugin tests fail on unrelated PRs. That wastes CI reruns and triage time, and it trains reviewers to ignore real `import-check` failures.

## How (Approach)

Lines 35-39 start `node -e "setTimeout(() => {}, 1000)"` with `budgetMs: 30` and assert `timedResult.process_signal !== null`. Likely cause (unverified; first reproduce it under CPU load): on a slow runner the 30 ms budget can expire before the child is spawned or signal-attributable, so no signal is recorded even though `state === "timed_out"` and `termination_cause === "budget"` are correct.

Make the child signal-observable before the budget can expire. Two options:

- Have the child print a readiness marker and wait for it before the budget clock matters.
- Raise the budget to a value safely above process spawn time, for example 500 ms, with a child that sleeps far longer.

Keep the existing `state`/`termination_cause` assertions. Do not weaken the `process_signal` assertion unless the manager's documented contract allows a null signal for a pre-spawn timeout. If it does, assert that documented case explicitly instead.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs`

## Acceptance Criteria

- The timeout case passes on 20 consecutive local runs: `for i in $(seq 20); do node --test .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs || break; done`
- It still fails if the manager stops terminating timed-out processes. Check this by temporarily disabling the kill path.
- The `import-check` plugin test job passes on the PR.

title: fix(full-loop): validate explicit commit-and-pr titles so workers cannot use issue numbers as task IDs
body:
## What

`full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --title "<title>"` keeps an explicit title as given, so a worker can open a PR titled `t<N>:` where `<N>` is the GitHub issue number, not a claimed task ID. Validate explicit titles before push: keep a `tNNN:` prefix only when it is a claimed task ID for this issue. When the prefix is the issue number, replace it with the derived prefix (`_derive_pr_title_prefix`) and warn. Otherwise fail before pushing.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-29/30 in a managed private repo. Headless workers on one runner handled lane-batch issues that carry no task ID and titled their data PRs `t<issue number>: chore: ...`, for example `t18815:` for issue #18815 and `t18803:` for issue #18803. At least six such PRs merged in a day.

- Issue numbers run ahead of the task counter, so `claim-task-id.sh` later allocated `t18802`–`t18804` to interactive work although merged PRs already used those IDs. issue-sync then warned `TASK ID COLLISION ... blocked by the dedup guard`, and the task had to be re-IDed by hand.
- issue-sync's PR-merge job completes TODO entries by the `^tNNN` in merged PR titles (see the t2720 note in `full-loop-helper-commit.sh`). A worker PR titled with an issue number can therefore complete an unrelated interactive task that holds the same ID.
- The rule already exists (`workflows/git-workflow.md:271`: issue-only work uses `GH#NNN`), and `task-id-collision-guard.sh check-pr` detects invented title IDs (GH#19987). But repos without that CI job never run it, and the commit-msg hook only sees commit messages, which repos with commitlint keep free of `tNNN`.

## How

- EDIT `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` `_commit_and_pr_prepare_metadata` (the `# Preserve explicit titles` block, about lines 229-232): when `pr_title` matches `^t([0-9]+):`, validate it before `git push`.
  - Accept it when TODO.md has `t<N> ... ref:GH#<issue>`. Reuse the matcher in `_derive_pr_title_prefix` (`.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-commit.sh`, about line 1314). Also accept it when the linked issue's title contains `t<N>`, matching `task-id-collision-guard.sh`'s linked-issue proof.
  - When `<N>` equals the issue number and neither proof holds, rewrite the prefix to `_derive_pr_title_prefix "$issue_number"`'s output and `print_warning` once.
  - Otherwise, `print_error` with the derived prefix as the remedy and return 1 before pushing.
  - `GH#NNN:` titles and titles without a prefix are unchanged.
- EDIT `.agents/scripts/commands/full-loop.md` and `.agents/workflows/full-loop.md` (section 4.2): one line stating that the `--title` prefix is validated and that issue-only work uses `GH#NNN`.

title: fix(release): print and classify Homebrew tap-check API errors so a quota blip does not fail publication opaquely
body:
## What

Make the `Check Homebrew tap state` step in `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml` diagnosable and rate-limit aware, so a transient API quota exhaustion does not fail publication with an opaque error.

## Why

The v3.39.88 tag-push publish run failed at `Check Homebrew tap state` (step 16) with only `Unable to determine Homebrew tap publication state`. The step captures `gh api` stderr into `TAP_JSON` (`2>&1`) but never prints it, so the cause is invisible in the log.

At the time of the failure (02:35Z), the maintainer account's REST core quota was 0 (reset 02:46Z), and the step authenticates with `secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`. A quota-exhausted 403 is the likely cause, but the swallowed error means it cannot be proven from the run log. `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` dispatched a same-tag recovery after the reset, and that run passed every step (GitHub, npm 3.39.88, Homebrew 3.39.88). Publication therefore needed a manual reconcile after a quota blip.

The same workflow already classifies installation rate limits for GitHub Release creation (`deferred=true`, step `Record deferred GitHub release`) and the postflight queue (`postflight_deferred`). The tap check has no equivalent.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.github/workflows/publish-packages.yml`: the `Check Homebrew tap state` step (`id: tap-state`, around line 368), and the `Verify Homebrew tap` loop (around line 404), which also discards `gh api` errors.

### Reference pattern

- The `github-release` step (around lines 180–200) and the `postflight-queue` step (around lines 430–465) in the same file grep the captured error for `API rate limit exceeded` and record a deferral instead of failing.

### Implementation notes

1. On `gh api` failure, emit a bounded, secret-free error class: the first line of the captured stderr, truncated, as `::error::` or `::warning::` text. Never echo tokens or headers.
2. Classify primary/secondary rate limits (`API rate limit exceeded`, `secondary rate limit`, HTTP 403/429 with a rate-limit body). Then either:
   - wait for a bounded period and retry (for example up to 3 attempts with backoff, within the job timeout), or
   - mark the Homebrew channel deferred (mirroring `deferred=true`) so `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` recovers it, and keep the publication summary accurate.
   Choose the option that keeps `release reconcile` semantics intact; deferral must never report Homebrew as published.
3. Keep non-rate-limit failures (404, malformed content, auth failures) as hard failures with the printed error class.
4. Apply the same error-class printing to the `Verify Homebrew tap` retry loop.

## Acceptance

1. A rate-limited tap check either retries to success or records a Homebrew deferral that `aidevops release reconcile <PR>` recovers, without a hard failure that has no reason.
2. Every tap-check failure prints a one-line, secret-free error class in the job log.
3. Non-rate-limit failures still fail the job.
4. Workflow lint (actionlint, if configured in Framework Validation) and the existing publish-workflow tests pass.

## Verification

- Existing workflow validation in CI (`Framework Validation`).
- Existing guards: `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-destination-state.sh` and `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-release-publication-workflows.sh`. If they assert the tap-check step shape, update them; add a rate-limit case there only if they already exercise step behaviour, rather than adding new test infrastructure.
- Release run evidence: the next tag publish shows the tap-check step summary line.

title: fix(pulse): release trusted-retry re-armed blocker holds within minutes, not the 3h LLM recovery interval
body:
## What

Release a trusted-retry or revision re-armed `status:blocked` hold within one or two pulse cycles, instead of waiting for the 3-hour LLM recovery interval.

## Why

`terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh` is the only path that performs the re-armed `status:blocked → status:available` release (`_tbr_release_circuit_hold`, reached from the per-entry check in `tbr_pending`). The pulse calls `pending` only from `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`, which is gated by `PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL` (default 10800s) and then only when an LLM run is due.

As a result, a deliberate OWNER/MEMBER `terminal-blocker-circuit:retry` on a retry-only class (`permission_required`, `push_policy_timeout`, `network_policy_timeout`, GH#35925) waits up to 3 hours before the issue is dispatchable again. The same applies to automated retry producers that post the marker.

Observed on 2026-10-30 in a managed private repo: an issue blocked at 01:20Z received an automated trusted retry at 01:52Z and was still `status:blocked` at 02:54Z. Eleven issues blocked by the v3.39.86–v3.39.87 shell-guard regression (GH#36017) needed a manual `gh-write-helper.sh issue status <N> available` after the v3.39.88 fix went live. The retry itself was already sufficient scheduling consent.

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/terminal-blocker-recovery-helper.sh`: add a mechanical-only re-arm pass (for example a `rearm` subcommand, or `pending --rearm-only`) that walks queued entries, performs only the existing re-arm check and `_tbr_release_circuit_hold`, and emits no LLM work items. Reuse `tbr_pending`'s per-entry logic (around lines 550–617) rather than duplicating it.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`: call the mechanical pass on its own short interval (for example a new `PULSE_BLOCKER_REARM_INTERVAL`, default 600–900s), independent of `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due`'s LLM gate. Leave `PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL` and the LLM supervisor trigger unchanged.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-discipline.md` ("Terminal-blocker recovery"): state the release latency and the new interval.

### Reference pattern

- `_pulse_blocker_recovery_due` (stamp file under `PULSE_DIR`, interval check) for the interval/stamp mechanics.
- `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_BUDGET_SECONDS` / `BLOCKER_RECOVERY_STAGE_SECONDS` for bounding the pass.

### API-budget constraints

- Skip an entry without the per-entry comment fetch when the issue's `updated_at` is not newer than the entry's last check. One issue read per entry per pass is acceptable; comment pages are not.
- Respect the existing secondary-cooldown and GraphQL circuit-breaker state; skip the pass while either is active.

## Acceptance

1. A queued retry-only observation with a trusted retry newer than the observation returns to `status:available` within `PULSE_BLOCKER_REARM_INTERVAL` plus one cycle, without an LLM supervisor run.
2. Entries without a re-arm signal are untouched and generate no extra comment fetches when the issue is unchanged.
3. The LLM recovery trigger and `PULSE_LLM_RECOVERY_INTERVAL` behaviour are unchanged.
4. ShellCheck clean; existing suites pass.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-terminal-blocker-circuit.sh`
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-recovery-policy.sh`
- Add a case to the existing terminal-blocker test for the mechanical pass (queued observation plus trusted retry gives release; no retry gives no write), using its existing fixtures and stubs.

title: t18800: fix(pulse): restore stranded worker drafts blocked by pre-v3.39.89 release projections

## Task


Pulse never revisits an issue that a pre-v3.39.89 worker release left `status:blocked` while the worker's draft PR is still open. GH#36019 (v3.39.89) stops new releases from doing this, but issues already stranded, and releases from runners still on older versions, stay blocked: the draft is never continued, merged or given attention. Add a bounded Pulse pass that restores `status:available` only when trusted evidence proves the block came from that release projection. The existing dispatch path then routes the draft to the bounded exact-head continuation (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-stalled`).

## Task Brief

## What

GH#36019 (v3.39.89) stops new releases from doing this, but issues already stranded, and releases from runners still on older versions, stay blocked: the draft is never continued, merged or given attention. The existing dispatch path then routes the draft to the bounded exact-head continuation (`pr-checkpoint-continuation-helper.sh dispatch-stalled`).

## Why (evidence)

On 2026-10-30, all three open `origin:worker` drafts in this repo were stranded the same way: PR #35984 (issue #35977), PR #35928 (#35918) and PR #35598 (#35592).

- The newest trusted coordination event on each issue is `CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_complete` from runner versions 3.39.84/3.39.85.

5. Project `status:available` through `set_issue_status` (releasing the runner's assignment). Post one audit comment carrying `<!-- aidevops:ops kind=draft-checkpoint-unblock pr=N release=ID -->` and log the result.
6. Run the pass from `_pulse_stale_blocked_sweep_repo` in `pulse-wrapper-cycle.sh` with its own completion stamp, on the existing 30-minute cadence and deadlines.

title: aidevops_bounded_operation kills long runs at about 2h despite a 24h budget_seconds
body:
## Observed

`aidevops_bounded_operation` `start` with `budget_seconds: 86400` ends with `SIGTERM` and then `SIGKILL` at about 7,200 s, long before the budget runs out. Four consecutive long runs of the same resumable import driver (OpenCode 1.19.x on macOS, aidevops 3.39.8x) all ended about 2 hours after they started:

| Run | Budget | Ended after | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 86,400 s | about 2h05m | SIGKILL |
| B | 86,400 s | about 2h10m | SIGKILL |
| C | 86,400 s | about 2h05m | SIGKILL |
| D | 86,400 s | 7,216 s | SIGTERM, then SIGKILL a few seconds later |

Status for run D just before the end: `state: running`, `remaining_ms: 79183554`, `progress_events: 0`, `progress_overdue: true`. Then `state: finalizing`, `process_signal: SIGKILL`, `containment: incomplete`, `post_exit_descendants_terminated: false`. The command printed its own interrupt line (it traps TERM), so TERM arrived first. The KILL came a few seconds later, before its cleanup (stopping a step on a remote host over SSH) could finish.

## Expected

The operation runs until `budget_seconds`, or the tool documents a lower hard maximum and rejects or clamps a larger budget when `start` is called. A termination before the budget also states its cause (for example idle or progress timeout, session or supervisor restart) in `status`.

## Impact

Long, resumable operational jobs (imports, media drains) lose up to an hour of work every 2 hours. Each kill also leaves remote state for the caller to recover by hand: a stale lock and a possibly still-running remote step, because the TERM-to-KILL gap is too short for the command's cleanup.

## Questions for the fix

1. Which component sends the signal at about 7,200 s: the operation supervisor (a `progress_overdue` / no-progress rule?), the MCP server process lifetime, or the host runtime?
2. If it is a no-progress rule: what counts as progress? The command wrote output lines every few minutes, yet `progress_events` stayed 0.
3. Give the command a configurable grace period (for example 60 s) between TERM and KILL, so trap handlers can finish.

## Files (likely)

- The bounded-operation supervisor in the OpenCode plugin (`aidevops_bounded_operation` start/status/cancel). Exact path not known from the caller's side.

## Verification

Start `bash -c 'trap "echo TERM at \$SECONDS; sleep 30; echo cleaned" TERM; while :; do echo tick; sleep 60; done'` with `budget_seconds: 14400`. It should still be running at 2h05m. When it is cancelled, `cleaned` should print before the kill.
### Files Scope

- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/bounded-operation-tool.mjs`
- `.agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/tests/bounded-operation-termination-cases.mjs`
- `.agents/reference/context-efficient-output.md`

title: fix(pulse): pause a runner whose own workers hit fast permission_required blocks on several issues
body:
## What

Add a runner-local circuit breaker that stops this runner from claiming new work after its own headless workers end several **different** issues with a fast `permission_required` terminal blocker. Today, one runner with a local permission/policy fault turns every issue it claims into a fleet-wide, human-gated `status:blocked` hold.

Also correct worker guidance so a private-processing `VAULT_POLICY_DENIED` that only this runner's operator configuration can clear is classified `runner_capability_unmet` instead of `permission_required`.

## Why

Observed on 2026-10-30, after v3.39.88 fixed the fleet-wide compound-shell regression (#36017):

- One device of runner `alex-solovyev` (OpenCode 1.19.4, aidevops v3.39.89) released six issues as `permission_required` between 03:11Z and 03:25Z. Each block came 1.5–2.5 minutes after the claim. This includes #36014: ready lease 03:19:48Z, blocked 03:20:50Z.
- One device of runner `vladimirdulov` (OpenCode 1.19.4, v3.39.88) did the same on #36015 at 03:11Z.
- Over the same window, the same runner's other device (OpenCode 1.19.5) finished three batch issues from the same private repository. It also ran one of the blocked issues for 3.5 minutes without a permission block (it then failed for an unrelated reason).

The fault therefore looks local to those devices. Each block still applies the issue-level `permission_required` hold. That hold re-arms only on a trusted maintainer retry. A faulty runner always has free slots, so it re-claims the next eligible issue within minutes. The blast radius is every issue it reaches before a human notices.

The terminal fingerprint (`v2:permission_required`) is only a class hash. It cannot distinguish SSH-grant requirements from runtime-policy denials, and the raw evidence stays in each runner's protected telemetry. The cause on those devices is **unproven**. This task bounds the blast radius by design and does not depend on that cause.

Retained local evidence also shows workers classifying `VAULT_POLICY_DENIED: unclassifiable_shell_read` as `permission_required`. These are records with reason `permission_required` whose detail starts "The runtime vault policy denied the initial worktree inspection". No grant flow can clear such a denial. The only remedies are relaunching under the operator's local-only binding or using another runner. That is the `runner_capability_unmet` contract: "Release for a capable runner … do not impose a global issue hold".

## How

1. **Breaker.** Follow the pattern of `is_no_work_rate_acceptable()` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-dispatch-gates.sh` (t2770). Add `is_permission_block_rate_acceptable()`:
   - Read this runner's own `~/.aidevops/logs/worker-progress-blockers.jsonl`. Count `terminal_blocker_captured` events with `reason == "permission_required"` and **distinct** `(repo_slug, issue_number)` in a rolling window.
   - Defaults: 3 distinct issues in 1800 s. Allow overrides with `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_BLOCK_WINDOW_SECS` / `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_BLOCK_WINDOW_MAX` (0 disables), plus the emergency bypass `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PERMISSION_BLOCK_BREAKER=1`.
   - When tripped, defer new claims for a bounded pause (default 3600 s, from the latest counted event), not just one cycle.
   - Log one content-free line to `$LOGFILE` containing only the counts and window.
   - Increment the `pulse_dispatch_permission_block_breaker_tripped` pulse stat. Surface it in `worker-activity-helper.sh` `pulse_stats`, next to `pulse_dispatch_no_work_breaker_tripped`.
   - Never read or publish dossier text. Never change labels or holds on already-blocked issues.
2. **Call site.** Call it wherever `is_no_work_rate_acceptable` gates dispatch (find with `git grep -n is_no_work_rate_acceptable .agents/scripts`), with the same "defer this cycle" semantics.
3. **Guidance.** In `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`, next to the existing runner-local lines ("A host-local lock or serialization guard …", around line 1099), add one line: a `VAULT_POLICY_DENIED` with check `unclassifiable_shell_read` or `classification_unavailable`, raised while working inside the worker's own worktree (the message asks for a local-only relaunch), is `runner_capability_unmet`. `protected_read` and `classification_mutation` stay `permission_required`. Owner-signed SSH or network grant denials also stay `permission_required`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper-dispatch-gates.sh`
- the single dispatch call site that already calls `is_no_work_rate_acceptable` (path to be confirmed with `git grep`; expected under `.agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh`)
- `.agents/scripts/worker-activity-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-lib.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/` — one new focused test for the breaker, modelled on the existing no_work breaker test (find with `git grep -ln is_no_work_rate_acceptable .agents/scripts/tests`)

## Acceptance

1. Three `permission_required` terminal-blocker events for three different issues within the window trip the breaker. The breaker returns 1 until the pause elapses, then returns 0.
2. Repeated events for the **same** issue, or events of other reasons (`unknown`, `runner_capability_unmet`, `files_scope_excluded`), do not trip it.
3. Setting `AIDEVOPS_PERMISSION_BLOCK_WINDOW_MAX=0` or `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PERMISSION_BLOCK_BREAKER=1` disables it.
4. A missing or malformed blocker log fails open (dispatch proceeds), and the error is logged.
5. No GitHub writes and no dossier or detail text in logs or stats.
6. The guidance line is present, and the existing `permission_required` guidance for protected-source denials is unchanged.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` on every changed shell file.
- The new focused breaker test, plus the existing no_work breaker test.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-headless-runtime-lib*.sh` (or the closest existing prompt-guidance test) still passes.
- After release, `worker-activity-helper.sh summary --since 6h --json` shows the new `pulse_stats` counter.

title: t18801: fix(interactive-session): claim must not silently skip when REST core is exhausted
body:
## Task


When GitHub REST core quota is exhausted (or REST is otherwise unavailable) at claim time, `interactive-session-helper.sh claim <N> <slug> --implementing` must still resolve the session identity through GraphQL and apply the claim. If the claim genuinely cannot be applied, the `--implementing` caller must be told with a non-zero, distinguishable exit and a plain warning, never a silent exit 0.

## Done when

- [ ] With REST `gh api user` failing and GraphQL `viewer` available, `claim <N> <slug> --implementing` assigns the session user and applies the claim status (regression test in `test-interactive-session-claim.sh`).
- [ ] With both REST and GraphQL identity unavailable, `claim --implementing` exits 75, writes no stamp, and prints a warning naming the issue and the re-run command; `interactive-start-helper.sh` surfaces "claim NOT applied" and continues.
- [ ] Regression guarantee: a confirmed non-maintainer (external repo) still exits 0 with no GitHub writes, and `lockdown`/`unlock` exit codes are unchanged.
- [ ] ShellCheck clean on all touched scripts.

Reference pattern: `dispatch-single-issue-helper.sh:1542-1560` `_dsi_resolve_runner_login` (REST first, then `gh api graphql -f 'query=query { viewer { login } }'`, login validated against `^[A-Za-z0-9]([A-Za-z0-9-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?$`, fail closed on malformed output).

Update the header comment (lines 123-132) to the new contract.
